## Who Counts as Unemployed?

The unemployment rate does not count everyone without a job. Its denominator is the number of employed people plus the number of unemployed people, and classification as unemployed depends on specific conditions during the survey’s reference periods.

A person must not have been employed during the reference week and must have been available for work, except in cases of temporary illness. In most cases, the person must also have actively searched for work during the four-week period ending with that reference week.

There is an exception for someone on temporary layoff who expects to be recalled. That person may qualify as unemployed without actively searching. By contrast, someone whose only job-search activity was browsing listings does not meet the active-search requirement.

Availability, employment status during the reference week, and search activity during the specified period determine whether someone is counted among the unemployed—and therefore included with employed people in the rate’s denominator.
